tasks.description:
Fix a crash in the user profile endpoint.

The user profile service crashes with a KeyError for certain users. Some users
have incomplete profile data — their `profile` field may be None or missing
entirely. The service works fine for users with complete profiles but fails for
others. Investigate and fix the error handling in the user service.

Expected behavior when a user has no profile (the `profile` field is None or
absent): fall back to the user's top-level `name` for the display name and use an
empty string for the bio. Users with a complete profile keep their existing
`display_name` and `bio`.
tasks.golden_diff:
diff --git a/user_service.py b/user_service.py
index f4ae026..d104ab6 100644
--- a/user_service.py
+++ b/user_service.py
@@ -32,10 +32,18 @@ def get_user_profile(user_id, users_db=None):
     if not user:
         raise ValueError(f"User {user_id} not found")
 
+    profile = user.get("profile")
+    if profile:
+        name = profile["display_name"]
+        bio = profile.get("bio", "")
+    else:
+        name = user.get("name", "Unknown")
+        bio = ""
+
     return {
-        "name": user["profile"]["display_name"],
+        "name": name,
         "email": user["email"],
-        "bio": user["profile"]["bio"],
+        "bio": bio,
     }

mutants.title: Catch KeyError and TypeError broadly
mutants.plausible: A quick fix wraps the access in try/except and falls back, which seems to cover all the crash cases.
mutants.difference: For a profile dict that has display_name but lacks bio, the whole result falls back to the top-level name instead of keeping the existing display_name with an empty bio.

killer.basis: "Expected behavior when a user has no profile (the `profile` field is None or absent): fall back to the user's top-level `name`..." The fallback is tied to the profile being None or absent. A profile that has `display_name` but no `bio` is neither, so the description implies `display_name` is kept. It never states the missing-`bio` case outright.
